```{python}
#| echo: false

# import packages
from itables import show
import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from functools import reduce 
from scipy.stats import zscore

import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# import data
physicians_per_1000 = pd.read_csv("data/sh_med_phys_zs.csv")
uhc_infectious_subindex = pd.read_csv("data/sh_uhc_sci_id.csv")
spi_pillar5 = pd.read_csv("data/iq_spi_pil5.csv")
spi_overall = pd.read_csv("data/iq_spi_ovrl.csv")
tb_incidence_per_100k = pd.read_csv(
    "data/all_forms_of_tb_incidence_per_100000_estimated.csv"
)
health_expenditure_gdp = pd.read_csv("data/sh_xpd_chex_gd_zs.csv")
```

```{python}
# Create a reusable function to tidy the datasets
def tidy_gapminder(df, value_name):

    df = df.rename(columns={"name": "country", "geo": "country_code"})

    id_cols = ["country_code", "country"]

    year_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.isdigit()]

    tidy = df.melt(
        id_vars=id_cols, value_vars=year_cols, var_name="year", value_name=value_name
    )

    tidy["year"] = tidy["year"].astype(int)

    tidy[value_name] = pd.to_numeric(tidy[value_name], errors="coerce")

    return tidy
```


```{python}
# Tidy every dataset
physicians = tidy_gapminder(
    physicians_per_1000,
    "physicians"
)

uhc = tidy_gapminder(
    uhc_infectious_subindex,
    "uhc"
)

spi = tidy_gapminder(
    spi_overall,
    "spi_overall"
)

pillar5 = tidy_gapminder(
    spi_pillar5,
    "spi_pillar5"
)

tb = tidy_gapminder(
    tb_incidence_per_100k,
    "tb_incidence"
)

health = tidy_gapminder(
    health_expenditure_gdp,
    "health_expenditure"
)
```


```{python}
# Filter to study years (Year 2000 and above)
datasets = [physicians, uhc, spi, pillar5, tb, health]

for i in range(len(datasets)):
    datasets[i] = datasets[i].query("year >= 2000")

physicians, uhc, spi, pillar5, tb, health = datasets
```

```{python}
# Merge datasets into one dataframe
dfs = [
    physicians,
    uhc,
    spi,
    pillar5,
    tb,
    health
]

# Use the reduce function to merge every dataframe in the list above
master = reduce(
    lambda left,right:
    pd.merge(
        left,
        right,
        on=["country_code", "country","year"],
        how="outer"
    ),
    dfs
)

# Since a full join was done, confirm missing values
# master.isna().sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
```


```{python}
# Considering the missing values associated with slowly changing indicators, use the "Most Recent Available Value" (MRAV) for them between 2020 and 2023. TB incidence, however, should remain strictly 2023 because it is the outcome variable and changes more meaningfully over time

# TB incidence (2023 only)
tb2023 = master.loc[
    master["year"] == 2023, ["country_code", "country", "tb_incidence"]
].drop_duplicates()


# Function to get the most recent non-missing value
def latest_value(df, value_col, start_year=2020, end_year=2023):

    temp = (
        df[df["year"].between(start_year, end_year)]
        .sort_values("year", ascending=False)
        .dropna(subset=[value_col])
        .drop_duplicates("country")[["country", value_col]]
    )

    return temp


# Apply function to the datasets
physicians_latest = latest_value(master, "physicians")
uhc_latest = latest_value(master, "uhc")
spi_latest = latest_value(master, "spi_overall")
pillar5_latest = latest_value(master, "spi_pillar5")
health_latest = latest_value(master, "health_expenditure")

# Merge the datasets
analysis_full = reduce(
    lambda left, right: pd.merge(left, right, on="country", how="left"),
    [
        tb2023,
        physicians_latest,
        uhc_latest,
        spi_latest,
        pillar5_latest,
        health_latest,
    ],
)

# Save cleaned dataset
analysis_full.to_csv("data/analysis_full.csv", index=False)
```

```{python}
# Prepare Health Security Preparedness Index (HSPI)

# calculate missing values
analysis_full.isna().sum()

# Remove countries without tb incidence. Since physicians and spi are core HSPI variables, drop rows with missing physicians
analysis = analysis_full.dropna(
    subset=["tb_incidence", "physicians", "spi_overall", "spi_pillar5"]
)

# Select variables and use z-score normalization to compress extreme values
variables = ["physicians", "uhc", "spi_overall", "spi_pillar5", "health_expenditure"]

for v in variables:
    analysis[f"{v}_z"] = zscore(analysis[v])

# Select z-score variables for HSPI
analysis["HSPI"] = analysis[
    ["physicians_z", "uhc_z", "spi_overall_z", "spi_pillar5_z", "health_expenditure_z"]
].mean(axis=1)

# Convert raw z-scores to 0-100
analysis["HSPI"] = (
    100
    * (analysis["HSPI"] - analysis["HSPI"].min())
    / (analysis["HSPI"].max() - analysis["HSPI"].min())
)

# Categorize Preparedness level
analysis["Preparedness Level"] = pd.qcut(
    analysis["HSPI"], q=4, labels=["Low", "Moderate", "High", "Very High"]
)
```


```{python}
# Calculate average HSPI and tb incidence
hspi_median = analysis["HSPI"].median()

tb_median = analysis["tb_incidence"].median()


# Create quadrants using hspi and tb_incidence averages
def quadrant(row):

    if row.HSPI < hspi_median and row.tb_incidence > tb_median:

        return "Priority"

    elif row.HSPI >= hspi_median and row.tb_incidence > tb_median:

        return "High Burden"

    elif row.HSPI < hspi_median and row.tb_incidence <= tb_median:

        return "Emerging Risk"

    else:

        return "Resilient"


# Create the quadrants for further analysis
analysis["Quadrant"] = analysis.apply(quadrant, axis=1)

# save dataset
analysis.to_csv("data/analysis_hspi.csv", index=False)
```
```{python}
# KPI VALUES

# Number of countries
num_countries = analysis["country"].nunique()

# Average HSPI
avg_hspi = round(analysis["HSPI"].mean(), 1)

# Average TB incidence
avg_tb_incidence = round(analysis["tb_incidence"].mean(), 1)

# Number of Priority countries
priority_countries = analysis["Quadrant"].eq("Priority").sum()
```
